units.context: "New Task" launcher button

units.source: This documentation is outdated, as it refers to using the deprecated __TRILIUM_PH_0__ API which will only create widgets for desktop.
units.context: "New Task" launcher button

units.source: Instead, a custom launcher widget can be created using the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Launch Bar Widgets__TRILIUM_PH_1__ documentation.
units.context: "New Task" launcher button

units.source: In this example we are going to extend the functionality of __TRILIUM_PH_0__Task Manager__TRILIUM_PH_1__ showcase (which comes by default with Trilium) by adding a button in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_3__  (__TRILIUM_PH_4__) to create a new task automatically and open it.
units.context: "New Task" launcher button

units.source: This uses the __TRILIUM_PH_0__Front-end API__TRILIUM_PH_1__ to create a icon in the __TRILIUM_PH_2__Launch Bar__TRILIUM_PH_3__, by specifying:

units.source: This portion of code is actually executed on the server (backend) and not on the client (i.e. browser).
units.context: "New Task" launcher button > Understanding how the script works

units.source: The reason is that the creating notes is the responsibility of the server.
units.context: "New Task" launcher button > Understanding how the script works

units.source: Here we can also see that it is possible to return results from the server execution and read them in the client (__TRILIUM_PH_0__).
units.context: "New Task" launcher button > Understanding how the script works

units.source: Here we identify a note with the __TRILIUM_PH_0__label__TRILIUM_PH_1__ __TRILIUM_PH_2__. This is how the __TRILIUM_PH_3__Task Manager__TRILIUM_PH_4__ showcase knows where to place all the different tasks.
units.context: "New Task" launcher button > Understanding how the script works

units.source: Normally this might return a __TRILIUM_PH_0__ value if no such note could be identified, but error handling is outside the scope of this example.
units.context: "New Task" launcher button > Understanding how the script works

units.source: We create a new child note within the to-do root note (first argument) with the title “New task" (second argument) and no content by default (third argument).
units.context: "New Task" launcher button > Understanding how the script works

units.source: Back on the client, since we created a new note on the server, we now need to wait for the change to be reflected in the client.
units.context: "New Task" launcher button > Understanding how the script works

units.source: Since we know the __TRILIUM_PH_0__ID__TRILIUM_PH_1__ of the newly created note, all we have to do now is to show this note to the user.
